dossier.architecture: Small swerve base, two-joint arm and pneumatic wrist/claw; early prototype robot used for software.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4i; compact base chosen around traffic and station chokepoints.
subsystems.intake: Pneumatic opening selects cone versus cube compression; rollers remain powered to retain pieces.
subsystems.transfer: Week-zero collector prototype was not yet installed; proposed four-bar would center cubes and upright cones.
subsystems.scoring: Shoulder/elbow joints with low gearboxes and MAXSpline transmission.
subsystems.controls: Profiled joint controllers, PathPlanner autos and separate practice/software robots.

versions: Day-ten functional prototype enabled early software. At week zero, the claw and proposed intake were still evolving; later Open Alliance posts must govern final configuration.
dossier.analysis: A functional early mechanism can buy more controls and driver iteration than a late, elaborate assembly. Do not mistake week-zero plans for the eventual Championship robot.
limits: Interview configuration and reported revisions are documented; full season chronology remains to be audited against the linked releases.

context_documents.body:
# 2023-3467: A week-zero prototype must not be treated as the final competition configuration

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The early double-jointed arm uses low gearboxes and MAXSpline transmission; the interview states roughly 100:1 at each joint. Pneumatic opening changes cone/cube grip. A proposed collector/four-bar was not yet installed in this snapshot.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team emphasizes getting a simple arm running early for software/setpoint work and describes profiled control for smooth repeatable movement.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A working early mechanism is valuable development infrastructure, but a proposed collector cannot become a fielded capability merely because it appears in the interview. Piece-dependent jaw opening also requires possession-state handling.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Verify later installed versions separately and test grip retention throughout profiled motion.

## Limits

Early snapshot only. Automatic captions are not sufficient to certify detailed motor/transmission part numbers.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/zqoVcHclGuM](https://youtu.be/zqoVcHclGuM)
